newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Material prices won't hit Tsingtao in H2.
newsitem.headline: Material prices won't hit Tsingtao in H2.

text.p: China's Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd said on Tuesday its profit in the second half would not come under pressure from raw materials price rises.

Raw material prices were expected to be steady in the second half after rising about eight percent in the first half of the year, and would not squeeze the company's bottom line, vice-chairman Peng Zuoyi told a news conference.

Last year Tsingtao's net profits fell 9.59 percent to 97.79 million yuan. Analysts blamed the fall on rising prices of raw materials and sharper competition in the domestic market, especially from new foreign joint ventures.
The company achieved 8.25 percent growth in net profit to 55.78 million yuan in the first half of 1996.

"Local beer still dominates the China beer market. Tsingtao Brewery...will not be threatened by competition from foreign beer," Li said. "On the contrary, we will learn from the sales and marketing techniques of foreign competitors."
The company's production stood at 203,000 tonnes in the first half, up 7.25 percent year-on-year. Its planned capacity for full-year 1996 was 426,000 tonnes.
The company, which some analysts said was not transparent enough, said it would make good this deficiency.
"Once decisions are made, we'll try our best to inform investors as soon as possible," Li said.
